evidence: src/application/list-tasks-use-case.ts: ListTasksUseCase declares `validateExecute(dto: CreateProjectDto): void`, which checks `typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === ""` and throws ValidationError("name is required"). It also imports `CreateProjectDto` from ./dtos, even though listing tasks has nothing to do with creating projects.

src/application/create-project-use-case.ts: CreateProjectUseCase.execute already runs the same check, `typeof dto.name !== "string" || dto.name.trim() === ""` → ValidationError("name is required"), on CreateProjectDto.
src/application/create-user-use-case.ts: CreateUserUseCase.execute repeats the same name check on CreateUserDto, so the name-required rule appears in three places.
All other use cases (AssignTaskUseCase, CompleteTaskUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase) keep to one concern per class through a single execute method.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module is cohesive: one use-case class per file, each with a single execute method, plus a shared dtos.ts. The exception is ListTasksUseCase. It has a public method, validateExecute(dto: CreateProjectDto), that belongs to project creation, not to listing tasks. Its body repeats the "name is required" check already in CreateProjectUseCase.execute, so the same invariant now lives in two places, and one of them is the wrong use case. That is both a split of concerns and a duplicated rule. The same trim-and-empty name check is also written out again in CreateUserUseCase. That is less serious on its own, but it confirms the name rule has no single home.

violations.message: ListTasksUseCase.validateExecute(dto: CreateProjectDto) is project-creation validation inside the task-listing use case. It copies the 'name is required' rule from CreateProjectUseCase.execute, so the module's one-use-case-per-concern boundary is broken and the rule now lives in two places.
The 'name is required' check in CreateProjectUseCase.execute is duplicated in ListTasksUseCase.validateExecute and in CreateUserUseCase.execute instead of living in one place.
